description: Machine-parseable registry of all known bugs with root cause analysis, regression test links, and pattern categorization.

root_cause_categories.path_error: Wrong file path or directory reference
root_cause_categories.schema_drift: Expected vs actual data shape mismatch
root_cause_categories.silent_failure: Error swallowed without logging or effect
root_cause_categories.mapping_error: Wrong value translation or type coercion
root_cause_categories.dead_code: Code that writes to a file or endpoint nothing reads
root_cause_categories.platform_compat: Code assumes one OS or runtime (POSIX-only modules, default text encodings, path separators, shell availability)

bugs.title: outcome_engine reads from wrong evidence path
bugs.description: outcome_engine.py read outcomes from .soma/outcomes.jsonl instead of the canonical .soma/evidence/outcomes.jsonl path.
bugs.pattern: Hardcoded paths diverge from actual evidence directory structure

bugs.title: outcome_engine expects wrong schema key
bugs.description: outcome_engine.py expected cells_used (list) but MCP tools wrote cell_id (string). Both schemas were valid in different writers.
bugs.pattern: Multiple writers produce different schemas for the same data, reader expects only one

bugs.title: sync.py silently ignores agent outcomes
bugs.description: sync.py did not map success/failure outcome strings to tp/fp counters. Agent-reported outcomes were silently dropped.
bugs.pattern: Outcome value vocabulary not shared between writer and reader

bugs.title: sync.py clobbers scores on missing outcome data
bugs.description: When a cell had triggers but zero tp/fp records, sync.py set score = 0.0 instead of preserving the existing score. Un-evaluated cells were treated as 100% failures.
bugs.pattern: Absence of evidence treated as evidence of absence

bugs.title: Dead-end .soma/cells/fitness.jsonl file
bugs.description: outcome_engine.py and cell_selection.sh wrote to .soma/cells/fitness.jsonl but nothing read it. The canonical evidence ledger was at .soma/evidence/fitness.jsonl.
bugs.pattern: Writer and reader disagree on canonical file location

bugs.title: diagnose_hot_zones.py uses Python 3.10+ type syntax
bugs.description: diagnose_hot_zones.py used dict | None union type syntax (PEP 604) which requires Python 3.10+. CI matrix includes Python 3.9, causing TypeError during test collection.
bugs.pattern: Type annotation syntax incompatible with minimum supported Python version

bugs.title: MCP server crashes on Windows: unconditional `import fcntl`
bugs.description: soma_mcp/tools.py (since v0.60) and soma_sdk/telemetry.py import fcntl unconditionally, so `python -m soma_mcp` exits with ModuleNotFoundError on Windows and MCP hosts get no Soma tools. v0.52 fixed this only in enzymes/fitness_updater.py.
bugs.pattern: Fix applied to one call site of a shared pattern, not to all of them

bugs.title: MCP write/execute tools unusable from MCP hosts: `_sessionToken` is only returned in serverInfo
bugs.description: Since v0.86 the server returns a per-process random token only as serverInfo._sessionToken and requires it as a tool argument for the 3 write tools and 6 execute tools. MCP hosts handle `initialize` themselves and don't pass serverInfo to the model, and the tool schemas don't declare the argument. So only the 5 read tools are usable, outcomes can't be reported, and fitness never evolves. Not platform-specific.
bugs.pattern: Auth handshake designed for a direct client, not for the host-mediated MCP protocol

bugs.title: Test suite writes to the real home directory on Windows
bugs.description: Running pytest on Windows (Git Bash) rewrote ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, created ~/.kiro (128 files), and overwrote ~/.soma/manifest.json and ~/.soma/backup in the real profile. Likely cause, not confirmed: install.sh resolves RESOLVED_HOME to the real profile instead of the test's temporary HOME. Knock-on: 10 test_install_lifecycle and 5 test_status failures. Not re-run on v0.88.2, because re-running would modify the real profile again. Related, confirmed on Windows: a python.org install has no python3.exe, so in Git Bash `python3` resolves to the App Installer stub. `command -v python3` succeeds, but running it exits 49 with no output. enzymes/common.sh install_hooks() therefore renders an empty hooks.json and skips hooks, and the other python3 calls in install/ and enzymes/*.sh fail. This does not cause the missing manifest: install_hooks runs inside an `if`, so set -e doesn't abort.
bugs.pattern: Test isolation relies on HOME overrides that the code under test does not honor

bugs.title: Windows PowerShell 5.1 cannot parse the PowerShell installers (no UTF-8 BOM)
bugs.description: install.ps1, install/install.ps1 and install/uninstall.ps1 are UTF-8 without a BOM. Windows PowerShell 5.1, which `.\install.ps1` runs on stock Windows, decodes them as cp1252. The em-dash's trailing 0x94 byte becomes a closing quote, so parsing fails and nothing is installed. CI misses this because validate.yml runs pwsh 7, which defaults to UTF-8.
bugs.pattern: CI tests a different runtime (pwsh 7) than the one users run (Windows PowerShell 5.1)

bugs.title: Implicit cp1252 encoding on Windows: `soma status` crash, list_cells garbles or silently drops cells
bugs.description: soma status prints emoji to a cp1252 console and crashes with UnicodeEncodeError unless PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8. soma_sdk/governance.py:89 calls read_text() with no encoding, so non-ASCII text comes back garbled. Inside `except Exception: pass` (line 95), any cell containing a byte cp1252 can't decode is silently dropped. Several tests in tests/test_rule_metadata.py also read files without an encoding (seen on v0.52).
bugs.pattern: Relying on the platform default encoding instead of an explicit utf-8

bugs.title: Windows-only test failures: path-separator assertions and verification contract tests
bugs.description: 3 tests in tests/test_init.py compare str(WindowsPath) against POSIX separators. test_mutation_tester::test_catches_tautological_test reports 0/2 survived on Windows, and 2 test_branch_coverage contract tests fail; cause not diagnosed. Not re-run on v0.88.2 because of BUG-010.
bugs.pattern: Tests assert on OS-specific string forms

bugs.title: PowerShell installer writes mojibake into generated rule files
bugs.description: With the parse failure worked around, install/install.ps1 reads rule files with Get-Content and no -Encoding (lines 223, 259, 280, 306, 428 and the Get-ContentWithoutFrontmatter callers). PS 5.1 decodes UTF-8 as cp1252, which put 54 garbled sequences into the generated CLAUDE.md (for example the three-character mojibake that replaces an em-dash). The PowerShell installer also skips hooks, so post-session fitness updates never run on native Windows.
bugs.pattern: Relying on the platform default encoding instead of an explicit utf-8

bugs.title: `soma checkpoint` / `soma sync` wipe cell fitness on a fresh clone (triggers→0, score→null)
bugs.description: The evidence .gitignore excludes fitness.jsonl (trigger events) while outcomes.jsonl (170 tp/fp records) is committed. On a fresh clone, aggregate_evidence returns triggers=0 with tp>0 for each cell that has outcomes. sync_frontmatter then overwrites `triggers` with 0 and sets score = tp/t, which is None when t == 0. Running `soma checkpoint`, which the pre-commit hook runs, reset all 41 such cells in a clean worktree of develop. A check command thereby rewrites tracked cell files, and a pre-commit run can commit the wiped fitness.
bugs.pattern: Derived state recomputed from a partially-versioned evidence set overwrites the recorded state
